facts.statement: The genus Apocopodon was first described from fossils found in the Danian-aged Marina Farinha Formation in Brazil.
facts.quote: It was originally described from the Danian-aged Marina Farinha Formation of the Paraíba Basin of Brazil.

facts.statement: Fossils of Apocopodon were recently reported in Kingstree, South Carolina, from the lower Paleocene Rhems Formation, expanding its known geographic range.
facts.quote: Recently, the genus was reported in Kingstree, South Carolina probably derived from the lower paleocene-aged Rhems Formation, significantly extending the geographic range of the genus.

facts.statement: The genus Apocopodon contains only one known species, A. sericeus.
facts.quote: It contains a single species A. sericeus.

facts.statement: Apocopodon belongs to the family Myliobatidae.
Apocopodon is classified within the class Chondrichthyes.
The time range for Apocopodon is listed as the Cenomanian to Maastrichtian, from 100.5 to 66 million years ago.
facts.quote: Time range: Cenomanian to Maastrichtian (100.5 to 66 million years ago)

rejected.statement: Apocopodon is an extinct genus of eagle ray that lived during the Paleocene epoch.
rejected.quote: Apocopodon is an extinct genus of eagle ray from the Paleocene epoch of the Paleogene period.
